key_insight: Generative diffusion models reconstruct missing cardiovascular flow information as ensembles of plausible fields rather than a single deterministic estimate.
engineering_relevance: Probabilistic flow reconstruction could augment incomplete cardiovascular imaging while representing ambiguity in unmeasured regions.
method: Train on a controlled digital-twin dataset of a healthy human left heart.
Generate unconditional samples of changing anatomy and flow across the cardiac cycle.
Reconstruct full 2D geometry and flow sections from partial observations, comparing ensembles with Gaussian process regression.
evidence_signal: On the digital-twin dataset, reconstruction means retained principal reference-flow features, while diffusion ensembles captured broader velocity and gradient fluctuations than the Gaussian process baseline.
watch_item: This proof of concept uses simulated healthy-heart data and 2D sections; performance on noisy in-vivo measurements and diseased anatomy remains unestablished.
paper_title: Augmentation of cardiovascular flow measurements with generative diffusion models
